fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10, whereas the target study concerns composition screening in the Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W refractory-alloy system.

It replaces the target intervention—rule-of-mixtures modulus validation, VEC/density screening of 38,326 compositions, and selection of Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5—with an unsupported GNN-CALPHAD-first-principles workflow.
It proposes tensile and fracture testing, while the decisive target experiment was room-temperature quasi-static compression of as-cast specimens.
It does not reconstruct the VEC-mediated dislocation-mobility mechanism or the tradeoff between retained modulus/strength and enhanced compressive ductility.
It provides no quantitative prediction of accuracy or computational-efficiency gains despite the explicit request.
No supporting evidence is cited, and no training set, feature representation, validation protocol, or uncertainty-calibration method is specified.
The benchmark lacks a defined blinded alloy cohort, preprocessing rules, comparator methods, sample size, and separate acceptance criteria for modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
explanation: The generated proposal is a generic machine-learning alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target methodology. The target validated a simple composition-based elastic-modulus estimator on roughly 130–132 HEAs, screened 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions using modulus, VEC, and density, and experimentally tested Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 against equimolar NbMoTaVW. It found 35.7 ± 0.9% compressive fracture strain, 1115 ± 18 MPa yield strength, and 2550 ± 75 MPa compressive strength. None of these design choices, conditions, mechanisms, baselines, or outcomes appears in the hypothesis. The stated reliability boundary is directionally reasonable but generic. A 10% MAE falsification threshold is nominally testable, yet it is not decisive without a prespecified external cohort, property-specific metrics, uncertainty handling, and comparison against the prior methods. With no evidence or quantified gains, the central claim remains unsupported.
